newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WRIGHT CHARGED WITH MISCONDUCT OVER "PERVERT" REMARK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WRIGHT CHARGED WITH MISCONDUCT OVER "PERVERT" REMARK.

text.p: Arsenal striker Ian Wright was charged with misconduct by the English Football Association (F.A.) on Monday over alleged remarks made about Sheffield Wednesday manager David Pleat.
Wright was reported in some newspapers to have called Pleat a "pervert" in the aftermath of the Arsenal-Sheffield Wednesday game at Highbury on September 16 which Arsenal won 4-1.
He has been ordered to attend an F.A. disciplinary commission on a date to be arranged.
Wright made the comment on September 27 and apologised three days later.
"It was just a joke. I didn't think it would come out that way," Wright said in a television interview on September 30.
Trouble started when Pleat called for an inquiry after Wright was caught by television cameras pulling the dreadlocks of Wednesday's Regi Blinker and stamping on defender Dejan Stefanovic.

The F.A. then wrote to Wright asking him to explain his comments, which referred to newspaper revelations nine years ago that Pleat was cautioned by police three times for kerb-crawling. The publicity forced him to resign as Tottenham manager.
